cross_industry.detail: TechSpot reported Nov 21 that TSMC and peers are expected to raise 2027 wafer prices by 10% to 20%+, with Taiwan IC design houses already notified and hikes effective Q1 2027; TrendForce expects foundry hikes of 5%–20%, most visible on 8-inch; TSMC was reported to set credit limits by customer financials, with cash payment required above the limit (not officially announced).

ACEA reported Nov 24 that EU BEV registrations in October reached 279,799 units, up 61.4% year on year, accounting for 29.8% of new cars; BYD sold 30,974 units (+128.1%), roughly three times Tesla's 10,166; six Chinese automakers together held a 14.8% share.

Lead times for large transformers have reached 3–4 years (about 1 year in 2020–2021), medium-voltage equipment over 1 year, and high-voltage circuit breakers about 125 weeks; nearly half of planned US data-center projects could be delayed or cancelled for lack of power infrastructure.

US Section 232 measures on solar take effect Dec 4, imposing a 15% ad valorem tariff on polysilicon and derivatives with a minimum import price ($21/kg for polysilicon); polysilicon spot prices were steady, with Bernreuter's global average at $5.79/kg on Nov 18, flat.

October PCE (consensus: core +3.2% y/y, headline +3.8%) and the second Q3 GDP revision (WSJ consensus +3.6%, Bloomberg +3.5%) are due Nov 25 at 21:30 Beijing time, after this briefing is delivered, so this issue only carries consensus; CME-based odds of a 25bp December hike rose to about 99% on Nov 24 (93% on Nov 23).
cross_industry.source: Morningstar, Nov 24, 2026; CME FedWatch methodology, Nov 24, 2026

meta.note: Wednesday briefing. Three top stories: the Ga/Ge/Sb suspension extended to Jan 27, 2027 (MOFCOM Announcement No. 59 of 2026, issued Nov 24), Nvidia gave back about $240 billion on Nov 24 (NVDA -5.86% to $155.38), and copper pulled back from highs (LME -3.5% to $12,054). Event library: 6 timeline entries added, 3 event titles corrected (Ga/Ge/Sb extension, ST price-hike confirmation, Siemens effective date Nov 1). Tier B batch 10: 11 subcategories, 3 with hits. Refrigerant spot: no verified Nov 24/25 range, so this issue's JSON omits refrigerant_spot (no stale values carried over).

siphon_effects.detail: Nvidia pullback: NVDA closed Nov 24 at $155.38 (-5.86%), giving back about $240 billion in market value in a single day; Schumer accused Jensen Huang of violating export-control law; the 10-Q delay is, according to UBS, linked to an ongoing investigation and whether additional risk factors are needed.

Applied Digital announced Nov 23 an 18-year lease with an unnamed Tier-1 hyperscaler for 150 MW of critical IT capacity, with base-term contract revenue of about $5.4 billion and about $12.7 billion including 33 years of renewals, with delivery starting in the first half of 2028.
siphon_effects.source: Company announcement via industry deal tracking, Nov 23, 2026

siphon_effects.detail: Korean media reported Nov 21 that most of Samsung's 2027–2029 memory capacity is already contracted, with some customers negotiating contracts through 2031 (Samsung officially confirms only that 2027 HBM is sold out); TrendForce cut its 2027 NAND total-bit demand forecast by 3.2% on Nov 17, bringing forward the forecast NAND contract-price downturn to Q2 2027; spot 512Gb NAND wafers were $14.267 on Nov 9, down 11.67% from Nov 2.
siphon_effects.source: Economy Tribune via TweakTown, Nov 21/24, 2026; TrendForce, Nov 17, 2026

siphon_effects.detail: Lead times stretched from 32 weeks at end-September to 40 weeks by mid-November, with some Samsung Electro-Mechanics models at 52 weeks; TrendForce expects the high-end shortage to run into the first half of 2027, with Q1 2027 price talks already underway in November.

Evertiq reported Nov 23 that FR-4 is already squeezed, the Nov 4 fire at Panasonic's Hukou plant threatens about 4% of global high-end CCL supply with no resumption date, and Panasonic is shifting capacity from standard FR-4 to MEGTRON and other high-speed laminates; HVLP copper-foil processing fees are up 30%–50% since December 2025; the conflicting 'seventh/eighth round' counts for Kingboard were clarified as a statistical-scope difference, with no new letter in the window.
No new orders or product announcements in the window; the Midea Vera Rubin partner claim is covered in Industry Updates item 2 (media report, not officially confirmed).

Nucor announced Nov 23 a hot-rolled coil spot price of $1,330/short ton (+$20) for this week, its 18th consecutive weekly increase, with lead times of 3–5 weeks; SMU's spot hot-rolled price was $1,390/short ton on Nov 17 (the Nov 24 current assessment was not verifiable behind a paywall, though the article confirms the uptrend continues) (Steel Market Update, Nov 23/24; SMU, Nov 17)

Evertiq reported Nov 23 that FR-4 is already squeezed, the Nov 4 fire at Panasonic's Hukou plant threatens about 4% of global high-end CCL supply with no resumption date; HVLP copper-foil processing fees are up 30%–50% since December 2025; Shengyi's November increases have landed (M6 +15%, PP +25%), with orders scheduled into January 2027; the Kingboard round-count discrepancy has been clarified, with no new letter in the window (Evertiq, Nov 23)

TrendForce cut its 2027 NAND total-bit demand forecast by 3.2% on Nov 17, bringing forward the forecast NAND contract-price downturn to Q2 2027; general DRAM is still +10%–15% for Q4, with conventional DRAM contract prices expected +5%–10% in Q1 2027; Micron says 75% of its 2027 supply is sold out; spot 512Gb NAND wafers were $14.267 on Nov 9, down 11.67% from Nov 2 (TrendForce, Nov 17)

MLCC lead times stretched from 32 weeks at end-September to 40 weeks by mid-November, with some Samsung Electro-Mechanics models at 52 weeks; KEMET's second tantalum-capacitor increase this year (Nov 1) was 20%–30% (T520 / T521 / T530 series); industrial-grade aluminum electrolytic capacitors (400–450V) stretched from 10–14 weeks in August to 18–22 weeks; Supplyframe's interconnect price index was 169.5 in October, forecast at 185.3 for November (+9.3% m/m, a forecast) (PCBA-HYH November guide, Findchips, Nov 12/17)

Supplyframe's interconnect price index was 169.5 in October (+1.5% m/m, +28.9% y/y), forecast at 185.3 for November (+9.3% m/m, the second-highest in nearly five years, a forecast); overall lead times are 12–21 weeks, with high-current power connectors at 22–32 weeks (Findchips, Nov 12/17, citing Supplyframe)

ST's fourth price-hike round confirmed: TrendForce reported Nov 24 that a Nov 4 customer letter raises prices on some products from Jan 1, 2027 (magnitude and part numbers undisclosed), with the first three rounds effective Apr 26, Jun 28 and Aug 23; NXP's third round (Nov 2 letter) and Renesas's second round (Sep 9 letter) both take effect Jan 1, 2027, unchanged; Infineon has no new letter this year, and its COO said Nov 10 that long-term delivery and capacity-reservation agreements with data-center customers now total over EUR 10 billion; onsemi has no new letter this year, with IGBT lead times of about 39–52 weeks (TrendForce, Nov 24; EE Times China)

Siemens's list-price adjustment is confirmed effective Nov 1 (SIMATIC PLC +5–20%, S7-1500 CPU about +15%, HMI +7–50%, SINAMICS drives about +9%, SIMOTICS motors +6%); the earlier Dec 1 reading had no source and is corrected; orders placed before the effective date must be picked up by Dec 31, 2026 at the latest; no new November letters from Schneider / ABB / CHINT / Delixi were verified in China (Excellent PLC check, Nov 24)

Lead times for large transformers have reached 3–4 years, medium-voltage switchgear 52–80 weeks, pad-mounted transformers 40–65 weeks, substation transformers 90–160 weeks, and large power transformers 160–210 weeks; nearly half of planned US data-center projects could be delayed or cancelled for lack of power infrastructure; grain-oriented electrical steel grade 120 averaged CNY 10,350/t on Nov 20, flat (Environment+Energy Leader, Nov 24; Mysteel, Nov 20)
